build: Rust release thinLTO codegen-units1 generic x86_64; no native target flag
method: 7 samples x128 batches; timings ns per batch; corpus all1296 square queries unless stated; kernel-only results do not establish search gains

R03.implementation: Inline five-square Free Eagle routes plus boxed-Vec overflow; generator running paths also inline. Move32→24B and MoveData24→16B; arbitrary JSON route lengths and encoded route order preserved. Clone not Copy.
R03.validation: 548 library tests pass plus new empty/1/5/6/40-square JSON and overflow storage regression pass. Final all-target/all-feature Clippy passes with one documented compact-layout box_collection exception.
R03.limits: Rust FreeEagle path variant now MovePath; accessor returns slice. Overflow has extra box indirection. Must measure whole search before accepting broad representation API change.

R08.implementation: Fixed heap Box<[Option<Piece>;1296]> squares and Box<[u16;1296]> slots; saves24B Board header.
R08.limits: Fixed Box clone code generation can differ from Vec memcpy; less metadata is not itself proof of search saving.

R04.status: measured kernel; not selected for production without integrated evidence
R04.implementation: Packed u64 endpoint clone/decode kernel plus prior complete ordered-route encoding parity.
R04.limits: New timing kernel isolates endpoint-only access, not full route identity/promotion spill/serde and public API migration. Cannot infer integrated gain from list copying.
R04.correctness: All paired checksums match at all6 corpus roots; geometry next/full-ray/mailbox also asserts ordinary blocker parity.
R04.disposition: Speculative / possible. Copying packed endpoints costs6.58% and endpoint decoding28.21% of the current Move-list kernels. Full ordered-route packing has prior parity evidence but is not integrated; no search saving claimed.

R06.status: measured kernel; not selected for production without integrated evidence
R06.implementation: Actual-position direct square reads compared with color-tagged slots plus dependent army lookup; same type checksum.
R06.limits: No integrated mutator/clone implementation; swap-remove and occupied/royal index maintenance must remain exact.
R06.correctness: All paired checksums match at all6 corpus roots; geometry next/full-ray/mailbox also asserts ordinary blocker parity.
R06.disposition: Dubious as a general read optimization: tagged-slot reads2.14% slower geometrically, with per-position ratios0.865–1.181. Sparsity changes the winner. Clone/mutation savings might offset this, but current search primarily makes/unmakes.

R07.status: measured kernel; not selected for production without integrated evidence
R07.implementation: Coordinate offsets→linear index versus u16 linear offset with explicit file/rank boundary checks; parity.
R07.limits: Both Position forms2B. Index encoding accelerates some indexing but makes file/rank reads, serde and file-major Ord compatibility costlier; kernel only one offset mix. All6runs repeat the same1296-square offset workload; differences across reported rows are timing variation, not board-phase effects.
R07.correctness: All paired checksums match at all6 corpus roots; geometry next/full-ray/mailbox also asserts ordinary blocker parity.
R07.disposition: Speculative / possible: linear-u16 offset/index kernel24.72% faster; same2B storage. Coordinate-heavy consumers, ordering and wire format must be accounted for before migration.

R09.status: measured kernel; not selected for production without integrated evidence
R09.implementation: Actual-position8B Piece AoS versus split position/type arrays; complete-use and position-only scans.
R09.limits: Detached scan kernel excludes multiple-array synchronization, promotions, swap-remove and lookup locality.
R09.correctness: All paired checksums match at all6 corpus roots; geometry next/full-ray/mailbox also asserts ordinary blocker parity.
R09.disposition: Dubious for movement-like position+type access: SoA scans3.42% slower even though color/promotion/origin fields are omitted, favoring SoA. Position-only scans1.62% faster with mixed per-position direction. No evidence supporting whole-board representation migration.

R10.status: measured kernel; not selected for production without integrated evidence
R10.implementation: All1296 squares x8 rays; repeated coordinate bounds vs20,736B next-index table vs300,720B full-ray payload, ordinary blocker parity.
R10.limits: Excludes Move emission, jumping/capturing-range restrictions, virtual overlays and added cache pressure during NNUE/search. No full engine claim. Counts include first occupied blocker irrespective of color; this is not legal-move enumeration.
R10.correctness: All paired checksums match at all6 corpus roots; geometry next/full-ray/mailbox also asserts ordinary blocker parity.
R10.disposition: Speculative / possible: next-square28.0% faster; full-ray31.0% faster for ordinary blocker counting. Actual generator emission, specialized captures, extra cache traffic and VirtualBoard semantics remain unmeasured. Incremental ray stepping is a smaller follow-up option.

R11.status: measured kernel; not selected for production without integrated evidence
R11.implementation: 38x38 sentinel mailbox ordinary ray walk with coordinate translation, checksum matches eight-direction baseline.
R11.limits: Excludes API coordinate conversion, large-jump padding, piece payload and existing sparse army/royal indexes; not a replacement implementation. Counts include first occupied blocker irrespective of color; this is not legal-move enumeration.
R11.correctness: All paired checksums match at all6 corpus roots; geometry next/full-ray/mailbox also asserts ordinary blocker parity.
R11.disposition: Speculative / possible: sentinel mailbox64.1% faster for ordinary occupancy-only ray walking. Kernel uses1B occupancy1444-slot mailbox; a real Piece payload board is larger and must preserve APIs, sparse lists and long jumps.

R12.status: measured kernel; not selected for production without integrated evidence
R12.implementation: Orthogonal visited-square counts using row/file occupancy u64 words versus square-by-square stepping; both include the first occupied blocker irrespective of color, with equal checksums.
R12.limits: Excludes occupancy maintenance, diagonals, capture class restrictions, virtual overlay updates, and Move emission. Large count-only wins remain speculative whole-engine savings.
R12.correctness: All paired checksums match at all6 corpus roots; geometry next/full-ray/mailbox also asserts ordinary blocker parity.
R12.disposition: Promising geometry kernel / production speculative: rank/file occupancy visited-square counts95.0% faster, with exact count parity including the first blocker. This is not a legal-move count: friendly/enemy endpoint eligibility is not modeled. Excludes update/overlay/piece-class/Move-emission cost. Existing rank-major occupied bitsets might support a smaller rank-only experiment without a full extra occupancy mirror.

R15.status: compiled complete descriptor-layout prototype + actual-position config-walk measurement
R15.implementation: Alternative enum mirrors every movement descriptor and recursively converts real configs, boxing40B Range blocker sets. Compiled enum shrinks48→32B, and full descriptor-walk checksums match at all6roots.
R15.limits: Current configs initialized once and borrowed. Moving blocker data adds indirection on capturing rays; no evidence yet that config footprint dominates. Full flatten rewrite beyond a quick safe trial. The workload uses for_piece_type, so promoted RainDragon/Whale origin dispatch is not modeled.
R15.correctness: All paired checksums match at all6 corpus roots; geometry next/full-ray/mailbox also asserts ordinary blocker parity.
R15.disposition: Reject simple blocker boxing: despite33% descriptor shrink, config walks21.16% slower (per-position14.7–30.4% slower). Full interning/static flattening might differ but is still speculative and needs a movement profile.

R16.status: measured kernel; not selected for production without integrated evidence
R16.implementation: Warm per-piece OnceLock lookup versus preinitialized direct config references on actual piece-type mix.
R16.limits: Direct-reference kernel is idealized. One global OnceLock still has an acquire check, while eliminating all runtime checks requires static tables/slices and special RainDragon/Whale handling; no startup or whole-engine claim.
R16.correctness: All paired checksums match at all6 corpus roots; geometry next/full-ray/mailbox also asserts ordinary blocker parity.
R16.disposition: Speculative / possible: preloaded config-reference lookup25.84% faster than warm per-entry OnceLock in the isolated lookup kernel. A single global runtime OnceLock still checks readiness, and building all configs eagerly adds startup work; it does not achieve this idealized path.

R18.status: measured kernel; not selected for production without integrated evidence
R18.implementation: One-capture Vec allocation versus inline Option payload for1296 captures per batch.
R18.limits: Kernel is best-case ordinary capture only. Correct production storage needs arbitrary capturing-ray spill; proposed inline-one/boxed spill may shrink Delta48→40B but needs real capture mix/whole-search parity and performance validation. All6runs repeat the same one-Pawn/1296-position workload; variation is timing replication, not capture-mix coverage.
R18.correctness: All paired checksums match at all6 corpus roots; geometry next/full-ray/mailbox also asserts ordinary blocker parity.
R18.disposition: Speculative / possible: inline ordinary one-capture payload costs7.1% of allocating Vec in the kernel. Production fallback for capturing rays, real capture frequency, clone/move size and API consumers are not measured; no search saving claimed.

kernel_probe.per_sample_statistic: mean ns per batch; reported value median of7 samples; ranges are min/max sample batch means
kernel_probe.note: Probe built against R08 fixed-array candidate, with original32-byte Move. Both sides of each kernel use identical board state. This isolates representation access/geometry; no whole-search claim.
kernel_probe.geometry_semantics: Visited squares along ordinary rays, including the first occupied blocker regardless of color. Counts model geometric ray traversal work and are not legal-move counts. Queries cover every square, not just current-turn pieces.
kernel_probe.replication_limits: R07 coordinate-offset and R18 capture-allocation inputs are identical across all6 runs: all1296 squares and the same single Pawn payload. Their six reported position rows are repeat runs, not independent phase-dependent workloads. Other kernel inputs vary with board occupancy, piece mix, or move list.
